keyVerseText: And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.
rootMeaning: The root of רַעְיוֹן (raʻyôwn) is רָעָה (râʻâh), which carries the sense of tending or shepherding a flock, implying close companionship and care. This origin suggests that רַעְיוֹן involves an intimate, active engagement, whether in desire or striving. Beyond the common English gloss of 'vexation' or 'longing,' the root evokes a dynamic relationship—either nurturing or consuming—highlighting the intensity behind the concept of yearning or frustration.
usageInScripture: The word רַעְיוֹן appears only three times in Scripture, consistently rendered with the idea of 'vexation' or 'longing.' The top translations—'also is vexation,' 'and of the vexation,' and 'and vexation'—indicate a strong association with emotional or spiritual distress. This consistency reveals that the term conveys not just general desire but a deep, often troubling striving or dissatisfaction of the spirit.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding רַעְיוֹן as both desire and vexation enriches our grasp of human experience in Scripture, showing how longing can be intertwined with frustration and restlessness. This duality points to the human condition apart from God—where our deepest desires often lead to vexation because of sin and the fallen world. Yet, it also invites believers to recognize their spiritual yearning as a signpost toward God’s ultimate fulfillment in Christ, who satisfies and calms the restless heart. Thus, this word underscores the tension between earthly striving and divine rest.
keyVerseReflection: Ecclesiastes 1:17 states, 'And I gave my heart to know wisdom, and to know madness and folly: I perceived that this also is vexation of spirit.' Here, רַעְיוֹן highlights the restless striving of the human heart seeking understanding apart from God. The term conveys that even the pursuit of wisdom, when disconnected from divine truth, results in vexation—a profound dissatisfaction and turmoil. This deepens the verse’s message about the futility of human effort without God’s guiding presence.
